ac.description: EX4100-F-48P as shipped - 48 PoE+ jacks, four Virtual Chassis and four uplink SFP+ cages, the built-in 850 W AC supply and two built-in front-to-back fans (Tables 14 and 26).

description: Juniper EX4100-F-48P is a fixed 1RU access switch with 48 10/100/1000BASE-T ports that all supply PoE+ (30 W by default), four 1/10GbE SFP+ Virtual Chassis ports and four 10GbE SFP+ uplink ports. The front carries the jacks in two stacked rows numbered 0 to 47, the two 2x2 cage groups, the chassis and port mode lamps, a Factory Reset/Mode button, a reset pinhole and a USB Type-C console port. The rear carries the management port with a USB port under it, the RJ-45 console port, the earthing terminal, an ESD point, two fans and the AC inlet. The 850 W supply and both fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays.

gaps.note: Table 15 and the callouts give the four Virtual Chassis ports as 1GbE/10GbE SFP+, while Figure 32, Table 25 and the Junos listing name them SFP+/SFP28 and give a 25 Gbps speed indication. The tables are used (10g); the cages are the same SFP-family cage either way.
gaps.wanted: Juniper's statement of the Virtual Chassis port speeds.

gaps.note: The Status lamp changes meaning with the mode button (Table 25), so the jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary and the mode lamps carry the meaning.
gaps.wanted: none beyond the component's own vocabulary.

gaps.note: The guide names the CLD lamp and sends the reader to the cloud-ready blink patterns, which it does not hold.
The claim code, serial number and CLEI labels are stickers with no content in any figure; they are named regions and are not drawn.
The earthing terminal is two bare holes for M5 screws. The library has no pair part for M5 holes on a 5/8 in pitch, so they are drawn as holes and no lug seat is offered.
gaps.wanted: a two-hole M5 earth terminal part

gaps.note: Only the 48-port CLI listing names the interfaces and the numbers are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

mgmt.mixed: how the switch is reached and restarted - the USB Type-C console, the reset pinhole and the mode button on the front, the RJ-45 console, the management Ethernet port and the USB port on the rear

airflow.note: Table 26 and Table 14 - two built-in fans with front-to-back (AFO) cooling, cold air entering the front vents and leaving the rear. The overview says back-to-front can be ordered but the guide lists no part number or figure for it, so no back-to-front configuration is modelled.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Tables 3, 14 and 26 and the rear callouts name a built-in 850 W AC power supply and two built-in fans, and Table 45 lists the switch "with in-built fans and power supply". The cooling overview says once that the fan modules are hot-removable field-replaceable units, but the guide has no removal or replacement procedure for a fan or a supply (its Maintain Components chapter covers transceivers and fibre only), names no part number for either, the rear callouts call them built in, and the photograph shows round grilles flush with the panel with no handle, latch or module outline. They are taken as part of the chassis, not bays and not components. The Junos listing in the guide shows a JPSU-920W-AC-AFO and fan trays for an EX4100-48P, which is a different box.

chassis.note: Tables 15 and 18 - height 1.72 in (4.37 cm), width 17.36 in (44.09 cm), depth 12.2 in in Table 15 and 12.26 in (31.13 cm) in Table 18, weight 5200 g. The centimetre figure 31.13 is printed in both tables, and 12.2 in (309.9 mm) is its rounding, so 311.3 mm is carried. The width is the body between the bracket fold lines; the guide gives no 19 in figure and the photographs show no ears.

colour.note: Median of the bare front face in the photograph, #acb1b6, and of the rear, #aaaeb7; the status plate reads #444b54. The face is carried at #a3a8af, a little under the studio light, as the library does.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's Figure 20 is the same studio photograph. The legends are drawn from the photograph: the model line reads EX4100-F in white and PoE+ in orange, the jack numbers are orange and the cage numbers white. The maker's logo and Mist AI mark beside the model line are not drawn and are reserved as a logo-zone.

earthing.note: Table 46 and Figure 96 - a protective earthing terminal on the rear panel for a Panduit LCD10-14A-L lug on two M5 by 10 mm screws, which are separately orderable. The photograph shows two bare holes on a lighter plate 15.7 mm apart (the 5/8 in lug pitch is 15.9) and no screws, so they are drawn as holes on the plate and no two-hole seat is offered.

lamp-size.note: The cage lamp windows are placed as common/led-arrow-sm@1 (2.0 by 1.75 mm). The photograph shows triangles about 2.8 by 2.6 mm, which common/led-arrow@1 (3.2 by 2.8) would match, but two of those overlap at the 2.95 mm step the photograph gives, so the smaller part is used.

mounting.note: Table 4 and the mounting topics - the 2-post kit SRX34X-RMK ships in the box (front-mounting brackets, two in Table 45), the four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK and the wall kit EX-WMK are orderable. The four-post kit also holds 2 in recessed front brackets, so a recess of 50.8 mm is the one measured position. No kit is listed under chassis.kits in this change, and none of the kit part numbers is modelled.

port-lamps.note: Figures 30 to 32 and Table 24 - each jack and each cage has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp. The jacks carry them in their keyway corners. The photograph shows four small triangular windows per cage column in the metal band between the two cage rows, two pointing down and two up; they are read as the two lamps of the upper port (the down-pointing ones, at 2.05 and 9.46 mm from the column edge) and of the lower port (the up-pointing ones, at 5.0 and 12.4), the left one of each pair being Link Activity by analogy with the jacks. No figure says which window is which, so the assignment is estimated. The Status lamp shows what the mode lamps select (Table 25), so its states cannot be one vocabulary here.

port-numbering.note: The legends under each column read 0 up-arrow, down-arrow 1, then 2 and 3 up to 46 and 47, so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The cages print 0 up-arrow, down-arrow 1, 2 up-arrow, down-arrow 3 under each group, and the right group is bracketed and labelled UPLINK. The left group is the Virtual Chassis ports. The numbers are as printed, from 0. Interface names are not printed on the metal. The guide's Junos listing for a 48-port model gives ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47 for the jacks, et-0/1/n, ge-0/1/n and xe-0/1/n for the four Virtual Chassis ports (PIC 1, 4x1G/10G/25G SFP/SFP+/SFP28) and ge-0/2/n and xe-0/2/n for the four uplinks (PIC 2, 4x1G/10G SFP/SFP+).

ports.note: Table 15 and Figure 22 - 48 RJ-45 ports in two rows of 24, in three shells of eight columns, then two 2x2 groups of SFP+ cages. Jack cavities centre at 15.75 mm for the first column and 348.2 for the last; the in-shell step is the registry's 13.97 and the shell step reads 117.4 mm, a gutter of 5.6. The rows centre 14.0 mm apart (14.1 on this photograph and 13.8 on the 48T's, the mean is used), the upper row turned 180 so that its keyway and lamps face up, as photographed. The cages are two columns by two rows, abutting on the registry's 14.25 pitch, at 360.1 and 391.8 mm; their rows read 14.7 mm apart and the registry's 15.0 is used.

power.note: Tables 14, 27 and 30 - an 850 W AC supply, 100 to 240 V, 50/60 Hz; at most 100 W input without PoE; the PoE budget is 740 W with a 87 W system budget, 827 W in all against the supply's 850. The budget is a separate figure and is not added to the 100 W. The rear legend prints 12A Max.

rear.note: Figures 21 and 23 and the rear photograph. From the left - the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB 2.0 Type-A port in one housing, the CON RJ-45, the earth symbol, a lighter plate with two bare holes, the ESD symbol and the ESD socket, two round fans at 135.8 and 197.1 mm, a label field and the AC inlet at 402.3 mm with its legend above (AC INPUT 100-240V 50-60Hz 12A Max, printed on the metal). Five screws stand along the lower edge. The label corner marks beside the console frame the claim code label (callout 8) and those across the middle frame the serial number and CLEI labels (callouts 4 and 6); stickers are regions and are not drawn.

reset.note: Figure 22 callout 9 - the reset button is the small round pinhole between the legends of the two jacks of column 22, at 334.3 mm, below the jacks. It sits between two legend arrows closer than the library's 4 mm button part is wide, so it is drawn as a pinhole in the metal and not placed as a part. The Factory Reset/Mode button (callout 5) is the blue one and is a part.

scale.note: Gate 1 - both photographs are straight-on studio shots. The front face is 1439 px across and the rear 1435, against 440.9 mm that is 3.264 and 3.255 px/mm; the rear's height of 142.5 px against 43.7 mm is 3.26 px/mm, 0.2 percent from the width, so the rear is orthographic. The front's bottom edge is lost in its shadow, so its y is read from the top edge at the same scale. The jack pitch reads 45.55 px, 13.96 mm, which is the registry's 13.97 mm on a quantity the scale never saw. Horizontal positions are measured from the centre of the face (the left and right edges disagree by up to a millimetre in the bevel) and every position is estimated, good to about half a millimetre across and one down.

sources.note: EX4100-F Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-10-01 (271 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4100-f/ex4100-f.pdf): Tables 3 to 5, 14, 15, 18, 21 to 27, 30 and 45, Figures 20 to 23, the mounting topics and the Junos CLI listing of the chassis hardware. Juniper's own straight-on studio photographs ex4100-f-48p-front-high.jpg and ex4100-f-48p-rear-high.jpg (1500 px wide JPEGs from the maker's public image library, no terms of use stated on the files), which supply every position below. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00150781enw) was tried once and did not answer, so no datasheet figure is used. Nothing of the guide or the photographs is copied here: every face is drawn new from measurements. No Visio stencil, 3D model or other held photograph of the EX4100-F was available, so none was used. End of life was searched 2026-10-22: no Juniper notice for the EX4100-F was found (a reseller tracker lists the EX4100 family as supported with no dates), so the lifecycle is none announced.

status-block.note: Figures 22 and 28 and Tables 22 and 25 - a dark plate at the right end holds the chassis lamps SYS, ALM, MST and CLD (left column) and the port mode lamps SPD, DX, EN and PoE (right column), each lamp above its legend, a round blue Factory Reset/Mode button with a list icon and the USB Type-C console (CON). The columns centre at 425.9 and 431.6 mm and the rows at 12.0, 16.5, 21.0 and 25.5. The lamps are very faint in the photograph and are placed from their legends.
